projects.list: Lists the projects in an organization; search filters by name or id. To also find branches, computes, or snapshots, use {{resources.search}}.
projects.count: Counts an organization's active projects without listing them; ones being created or deleted are not counted.
projects.get: Gets a project's settings, default compute settings, history retention, owner, and usage. For branches, use {{branches.list}}.
projects.update: Updates a project's name, settings, default compute settings, or history retention.
projects.delete: Deletes a project with all its branches, computes, databases, and roles. NEVER run autonomously; always ask the user first. {{projects.recover}} undoes it within 7 days. For one branch, use {{branches.delete}}.
projects.recover: Recovers a project deleted in the last 7 days; {{projects.list}} with recoverable true finds them. Some integrations need setting up again.
projects.transfer: Moves projects from one organization to another. The API key needs access to both organizations.
projects.transferFromUser: Deprecated: personal accounts are now organizations. Use {{projects.transfer}}.
projects.permissions.list: Lists who has access to a project: each permission id, email, and grant date.
projects.permissions.grant: Gives the Neon account with this email access to a project.
projects.permissions.revoke: Removes one person's access to a project.
projects.members.list: Lists organization members and their roles on an org-owned project; 404 when the project is not org-owned or per-project roles are off.
projects.members.setRole: Sets an organization member's explicit role on a project. Idempotent.
projects.members.removeRole: Removes an organization member's explicit role on a project; their organization role's project access remains. Idempotent.
branches.list: Lists a project's branches with id (br-...), name, parent, and default flag; search finds a branch's id by name.
branches.get: Gets a branch record: name, parent, state, protection, size, and timestamps. For its databases and tables, use {{branches.describe}}.
branches.update: Renames a branch, protects or unprotects it, or sets when it expires.
branches.delete: Deletes a branch with all its data and disconnects its clients. NEVER run autonomously; always ask the user first. The root, the default, and a branch with children cannot be deleted. For the whole project, use {{projects.delete}}.
branches.setDefault: Makes a branch the project's default; the previous default loses the flag.
branches.finalizeRestore: Finalizes a branch restored with finalize false: moves the original branch's computes onto it, restarting them, and takes over its name.
postgres.endpoints.list: Lists the compute endpoints of every branch in a project. For one branch, use {{postgres.endpoints.listByBranch}}.
postgres.endpoints.listByBranch: Lists a branch's compute endpoints. For every branch in the project, use {{postgres.endpoints.list}}.
postgres.endpoints.get: Gets a compute endpoint (ep-...): host, type, state, and autoscaling limits.
postgres.endpoints.create: Creates a compute endpoint on a branch; a branch takes one read-write endpoint and any number of read-only. Returns no connection string; use {{postgres.connectionString}}.
postgres.endpoints.delete: Deletes a compute endpoint and drops its connections.
postgres.endpoints.suspend: Suspends a compute endpoint, dropping its connections.
postgres.endpoints.restart: Restarts a compute endpoint by suspending and starting it, dropping its connections.
postgres.roles.get: Gets a Postgres role on a branch.
postgres.roles.delete: Deletes a Postgres role from a branch.
postgres.roles.resetPassword: Sets a new random password for a Postgres role and returns it. Drops the compute's connections.
postgres.databases.list: Lists a branch's databases and their owners.
postgres.databases.get: Gets a database on a branch and its owner.
postgres.databases.create: Creates a database on a branch, owned by owner_name.
postgres.databases.update: Renames a database or changes its owner.
postgres.databases.delete: Deletes a database and its data from a branch.
postgres.dataApi.get: Gets the Neon Data API configuration for one database on a branch: endpoint URL, state, and settings.
postgres.dataApi.create: Creates the Neon Data API, a REST interface over database_name, on a branch.
postgres.dataApi.update: Updates the Neon Data API settings for a database and refreshes its schema cache.
postgres.dataApi.delete: Deletes the Neon Data API for a database; requests to its endpoint start failing.
storage.get: Checks whether object storage is available on a branch; a 404 says why not.
storage.buckets.list: Lists a branch's object storage buckets, inherited ones included.
storage.buckets.create: Creates an object storage bucket on a branch.
storage.buckets.delete: Deletes a bucket from a branch.
storage.objects.list: Lists a bucket's objects on a branch, inherited ones included.
storage.objects.delete: Deletes one object from a bucket on a branch.
storage.objects.deleteByPrefix: Soft-deletes every object on this branch whose key starts with prefix and returns the count; inherited objects stay.
storage.objects.presign: Returns a short-lived presigned PUT or GET URL for one object, with the headers to send; no S3 credentials needed.
functions.list: Lists the functions on a branch.
functions.get: Gets a function on a branch by slug.
functions.update: Sets a function's display name; null resets it to the slug. Only the branch that owns the function can rename it.
functions.delete: Deletes a function from a branch.
functions.deploy: Deploys a function version from any of zip, environment, and runtime; omitted ones keep the latest value, and the first deployment needs zip. It can return while still pending.
functions.customDomains.list: Lists a branch's custom domains and their targets.
functions.customDomains.register: Routes a domain you own to a function: entity_type function, entity_id the slug from {{functions.list}}. It goes live once a CNAME to the returned cname_target resolves.
functions.customDomains.delete: Removes a custom domain from a branch and stops routing it.
triggers.list: Lists a branch's function triggers, including inherited ones, which stay disabled on this branch until enabled.
triggers.get: Gets a function trigger on a branch.
triggers.create: Creates a trigger that calls a function on a five-field UTC cron schedule, or after an upload to one bucket, optionally under a key prefix. Names are unique on the branch.
triggers.update: Updates a function trigger; body.type must match its kind. Editing an inherited trigger makes a local copy, disabled unless this request enables it.
triggers.delete: Deletes a function trigger, or hides an inherited one on this branch. Invocations already queued still run.
credentials.list: Lists the scoped credentials issued on a branch, without secrets.
credentials.create: Issues a scoped credential on a branch. api_token and s3_secret_access_key are returned once: show them to the user and tell them to store them.
credentials.rotate: Replaces a scoped credential's secrets in place and returns them once; token_id stays. Not idempotent: if the response is lost, create a new credential ({{credentials.create}}) and revoke this one instead of retrying.
aiGateway.get: Gets a branch's AI Gateway host; a 404 says why it is unavailable.
realtime.get: Gets a branch's Realtime state, URL, and allowed origins; the secret comes from {{realtime.secret}}.
realtime.enable: Enables Realtime on a branch, or changes its allowed origins, and waits until it is applied.
realtime.disable: Disables Realtime on a branch, discarding its secret, and waits until it is applied.
realtime.secret: Gets the secret the application backend issues Realtime tokens with; 404 until {{realtime.enable}} has run.
realtime.rotateSecret: Replaces a branch's Realtime secret and waits until the old one stops working. NEVER run autonomously; always ask the user first. Then update the application backend from {{realtime.secret}}.
logs.query: Returns a branch's log records. Filters combine with AND; pass logql or structured filters, not both. Pass since or start_time, not both; default last hour, max seven days. Private beta: a branch without logs returns 404 telemetry_not_enabled. Stream labels: {{logs.loki.queryRange}}.
logs.fields: Lists the low-cardinality log fields seen on a branch, for {{logs.fieldValues}}.
logs.fieldValues: Lists the distinct values of one log field; a field the branch never emitted returns unknown_field. Pass since or start_time, not both; default last six hours, max seven days.
snapshots.create: Creates a snapshot of a branch.
snapshots.update: Renames a snapshot or changes when it expires.
snapshots.getSchedule: Gets a branch's automatic snapshot schedule.
operations.list: Lists a project's operations; ones older than six months may be gone.
operations.get: Gets one operation: its action, status, and error.
auth.get: Gets a branch's Neon Auth integration record: provider, base URL, JWKS URL, and database. Prefer {{auth.getConfig}}, which adds the auth settings, unless you only need the record.
auth.create: Enables Neon Auth on a branch and creates the neon_auth schema in its database.
auth.disable: Disables Neon Auth on a branch. delete_data also drops the neon_auth schema and its tables.
auth.updateConfig: Sets the application name Neon Auth uses in its emails.
auth.oauthProviders.list: Lists the social login providers (Google, GitHub, Microsoft, Vercel, Apple) of a branch's Neon Auth. For Neon Auth as an OAuth server, use {{auth.oauthServer.get}}.
auth.oauthProviders.add: Adds a social login provider to a branch's Neon Auth. Microsoft and Apple need your own client_id and client_secret; for Apple these are the Services ID and .p8 key, plus apple_team_id and apple_key_id.
auth.oauthProviders.update: Updates a social login provider on a branch's Neon Auth. For Apple, send a new client_secret (.p8 key) together with its apple_key_id.
auth.oauthProviders.delete: Removes a social login provider from a branch's Neon Auth.
auth.oauthServer.get: Gets a branch's Neon Auth OAuth 2.1 server settings (oauth_provider plugin), for example for MCP clients. For social login, use {{auth.oauthProviders.list}}.
auth.oauthServer.update: Configures a branch's Neon Auth as an OAuth 2.1 server (oauth_provider plugin); root branch only. Enabling needs login_page, consent_page, and a resource or MCP resource. resources replaces the stored list, so send the full list from {{auth.oauthServer.get}}. mcp needs mcp.resource; mcp.resource "" removes it.
auth.oauthClients.list: Lists the OAuth clients (apps, MCP clients) of a branch's Neon Auth OAuth server, without secrets; not social login providers.
auth.oauthClients.get: Gets an OAuth client of a branch's Neon Auth OAuth server, without its secret.
auth.oauthClients.create: Registers an OAuth client with a branch's Neon Auth OAuth server. A confidential client's client_secret is returned once: show it to the user and tell them to store it. resources must already be on the server ({{auth.oauthServer.get}}). type is permanent.
auth.oauthClients.update: Updates an OAuth client of Neon Auth's OAuth server; redirect_uris and resources replace the stored lists, and type cannot change.
auth.oauthClients.delete: Deletes an OAuth client from Neon Auth's OAuth server, irreversibly; tokens already issued stay valid.
auth.oauthClients.rotateSecret: Issues a new secret for a confidential OAuth client; the old one stops working at once. The new client_secret is returned once: show it to the user and tell them to store it.
auth.trustedDomains.list: Lists the domains a branch's Neon Auth may redirect to after sign-in.
auth.trustedDomains.add: Adds a domain a branch's Neon Auth may redirect to after sign-in.
auth.trustedDomains.delete: Removes a domain from the ones a branch's Neon Auth may redirect to.
auth.users.create: Creates a Neon Auth user on a branch who can sign in right away.
auth.users.delete: Deletes a Neon Auth user from a branch. Irreversible.
auth.users.updateRole: Sets the roles of a Neon Auth user on a branch.
auth.allowLocalhost.get: Gets whether a branch's Neon Auth accepts localhost origins.
auth.allowLocalhost.update: Sets whether a branch's Neon Auth accepts localhost origins; turn it off for production. Current value: {{auth.getConfig}}.
auth.emailAndPassword.get: Gets a branch's Neon Auth email and password sign-in settings.
auth.emailAndPassword.update: Updates a branch's Neon Auth email and password sign-in; omitted fields keep their value. Current values: {{auth.getConfig}}.
auth.emailProvider.get: Gets a branch's Neon Auth email provider; the SMTP password comes back empty.
auth.emailProvider.update: Sets the email provider for Neon Auth's emails: body.type "shared" for Neon's sender, or "standard" with your SMTP details. Test it with {{auth.emailProvider.sendTest}}.
auth.emailProvider.sendTest: Sends a test email through the branch's saved SMTP provider to recipient_email. Only send to an address the user gave you. A failed send returns success false with error_message, not an error.
auth.plugins.get: Gets all Neon Auth plugin settings of a branch in one response. OAuth and SMTP secrets come back empty.
auth.plugins.magicLink.update: Updates the Neon Auth magic link plugin; omitted fields keep their value. Current values: {{auth.getConfig}}.
auth.plugins.organization.update: Updates the Neon Auth organization plugin, which lets your app's users form organizations (not Neon organizations). Omitted fields keep their value.
auth.plugins.phoneNumber.get: Gets a branch's Neon Auth SMS OTP plugin settings.
auth.plugins.phoneNumber.update: Updates the Neon Auth SMS OTP plugin; omitted fields keep their value. SMS needs a webhook with the send.otp event ({{auth.webhooks.update}}).
auth.webhooks.get: Gets a branch's Neon Auth webhook: URL, enabled events, and timeout.
auth.webhooks.update: Replaces a branch's Neon Auth webhook configuration; omitted fields reset, so { enabled: false } alone clears webhook_url and enabled_events. Send every field to keep, read from {{auth.getConfig}}.
consumption.perProject: Returns per-project consumption on legacy Scale, Business, and Enterprise billing. For current plans, use {{consumption.perProjectV2}}.
consumption.perProjectV2: Returns per-project consumption in an organization. metrics: every name {{consumption.perBranchV2}} takes, plus extra_branches_month and snapshot_storage_bytes_month. Launch, Scale, Agent, Business, or Enterprise plans; others get 403.
consumption.perBranchV2: Returns per-branch consumption for project_ids. metrics: compute_unit_seconds, root_branch_bytes_month, child_branch_bytes_month, instant_restore_bytes_month, public_network_transfer_bytes, private_network_transfer_bytes, functions_active_capacity_microseconds, functions_waiting_capacity_microseconds, functions_invocations, functions_egress_bytes. Usage-based Launch, Scale, Agent, or Enterprise plans only.
apiKeys.list: Lists your personal API keys, without tokens. An organization API key gets 404; use {{organizations.apiKeys.list}}.
apiKeys.create: Creates a personal API key. The key is returned once: show it to the user and tell them to store it.
apiKeys.revoke: Revokes a personal API key. Irreversible.
organizations.get: Gets an organization's name, plan, and settings.
organizations.members.list: Lists an organization's members and their roles.
organizations.members.get: Gets an organization member and their role.
organizations.members.update: Changes an organization member's role. Admins only.
organizations.members.remove: Removes a member from an organization. Admins only; the last admin cannot be removed.
organizations.invitations.list: Lists an organization's pending and accepted invitations.
organizations.invitations.create: Invites people to an organization by email; existing Neon users join at once, others are asked to sign up.
organizations.spendingLimit.get: Gets an organization's monthly spending limit (spending_limit_cents null means none). Launch and Scale only.
organizations.spendingLimit.set: Sets an organization's monthly spending limit; Neon emails at 80% and 100% and never suspends computes. Admins on Launch and Scale only.
organizations.spendingLimit.delete: Removes an organization's monthly spending limit. Idempotent.
organizations.apiKeys.list: Lists an organization's API keys, without their tokens.
organizations.apiKeys.create: Creates an organization API key, optionally limited to one project. The key is returned once: show it to the user and tell them to store it.
organizations.apiKeys.revoke: Revokes an organization API key. Irreversible.
user.me: Gets the authenticated Neon user: ids, plan, and linked login accounts. An organization API key gets 404.
